drafted_from: workflow:port-without-losing-anything's row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (its job, input schema and the step named in the worked example)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:port-without-losing-anything: the Orders page of the old admin at https://old.example.com/admin moves to the Orders screen of the new dashboard at https://app.example.com/orders."
no_lists_because: It compares what one screen lets a person do against another and keeps the answers in the run itself, so it reads and writes no list.
instructions: 1. Name where the old one is and where it moves to, for example "https://old.example.com/admin/orders" and "https://app.example.com/orders", and say "Run workflow:port-without-losing-anything" with old and new (each at least 3 characters).
2. At inventory, use the old one yourself and list at least 3 capabilities, including what only shows on hover, selection or right-click, each with an id, what it does and how it is reached.
3. At check, try each in the new home the way a person would and mark it there, missing or worse.
4. At restore, bring back each missing or worse one through the shared parts, not a one-off copy, and attach before and after pictures of old and new.

worked_examples.title: List what the old Orders page let a person do
worked_examples.ask: Run workflow:port-without-losing-anything: the old admin Orders page moves to the new dashboard.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json, step inventory: its submit shape is capabilities, at least 3 items each with id, what (at least 5 characters) and how_reached (at least 3 characters). The old page is used by hand for the list below.
